# frostmoln_appgw_waf_platform_rules (Data Source)

The **platform-owned** rules in an Application Gateway WAF policy: the gateway's own self-protection, and any emergency virtual patch in force.

Read-only. You cannot create, edit or delete one. Where `opt_out_allowed` is true you may turn it off for this gateway — which is the one write a tenant may make to a rule they do not own, and is not expressible in Terraform today; use `fm appgw waf rule opt-out` or the portal.

Worth reading in a configuration to assert on: a rule appearing here that you did not expect is the platform having shipped a patch, which is exactly the thing to notice.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The platform's own rules: gateway self-protection, and any emergency virtual
# patch in force. Read-only.
#
# Worth asserting on: a rule appearing here that you did not expect is the
# platform having shipped a patch, which is exactly the thing to notice.

data "frostmoln_appgw_waf_platform_rules" "in_force" {
  gateway_id = frostmoln_application_gateway.edge.id
  policy_id  = frostmoln_appgw_waf_policy.main.id
}

output "platform_patches_i_have_opted_out_of" {
  value = [
    for r in data.frostmoln_appgw_waf_platform_rules.in_force.rules :
    r.rule_key if r.opted_out
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `gateway_id` (String) The Application Gateway the policy belongs to.
- `policy_id` (String) The WAF policy to read.

### Optional

- `source` (String) Which ruleset to read: `draft` (default) is what is being edited, `active` is what the gateway is enforcing. They differ whenever there are unpublished changes, which is most of the time during an apply.

### Read-Only

- `rules` (Attributes List) The rules, in evaluation order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `version` (Number) The version number the returned rules came from.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Read-Only:

- `builder_json` (String) The structured body as JSON, for a builder rule.
- `description` (String) What the rule is for.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is evaluated.
- `kind` (String) `builder`, `raw` or `managedOverride`.
- `managed_action` (String) `disable` or `updateTarget`.
- `managed_secrule_id` (Number) The managed rule an override applies to.
- `managed_target` (String) The replacement target.
- `opt_out_allowed` (Boolean) For a platform rule: whether it may be turned off at all. Gateway self-protection rules may not.
- `opted_out` (Boolean) For a platform rule: whether this tenant has turned it off.
- `ordinal` (Number) Evaluation order within the policy.
- `owner` (String) `tenant` or `platform`.
- `raw` (String) The SecLang text, for a raw rule.
- `revision` (Number) The server-assigned write counter.
- `rule_key` (String) The rule's stable identity.
- `secrule_id` (Number) The SecRule id the platform assigned.
